items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: before he died, the father of Dexter Gordon, he promised me that if ever there was a time that I could do anything to help his son, to do so.

ctx.x: And he -- this doctor was a lover of music. So he took a very good liking to my father and my mother and he gave special care to me and he would, even though he was overburdened with patients during this time of the big epidemic -- it was almost a plague -- in 1918, he made sure that he got by my house once or twice everyday to make special care that I was able to get along with it and get over with it.

So, after many years, he bore a son by the name of Dexter Gordon and I was -- before he died, the father of Dexter Gordon, he promised me that if ever there was a time that I could do anything to help his son, to do so. I had a chance to

repay him for his kindnesses when Lionel Hampton first started his band in 1940. In the fall of 1940, we had an empty spot in the saxophone section and his son Dexter was coming up, was a young teenager -- he was about 15, 16 years old -- and he wanted to play. So I got a chance to repay his dad for all of his kindness by getting Dexter on the Lionel Hampton Band, which was the first band that Dexter Gordon ever worked with. He went right on from there.
